title: Ultrasound Diagnostic System, Hand Carried (USHC) - Prototype
description: 4 NOV 2026 - The purpose of this revision is to incorporate Revision 1 of the RPP, upload the Questions and Answers and to extend the offeror due date to 1600 EST, 20 November 2026. With the incorporation of this revision, final questions are due NLT 1600 EST, 9 November 2026. A follow on Questions and Answers for this period will be uploaded shortly after 9 November 2026. Three attachments will be uploaded in this RPP revision: 1) W91CRB-RPP-USHC_Rev 1 - changes are highlighted in red font to the following sections of the RPP: Sections 2.4, 5.1 & 5.2 2) W91CRB-RPP-USHC_QAs - .pdf containing 10 questions and answers 3) W91CRB-RPP-USHC_QAs_Cont. - Excel spreadsheet containing remaining questions ****************************************************************************************************************************************************** The Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Maneuver Ground Project Manager (PM) Maneuver Medical Devices (M2S) is issuing this Request for Prototype Proposals (RPP) to solicit solutions for an Ultrasound Diagnostic System, Hand Carried (USHC). The U.S. Army requires a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) or Non-Developmental Item (NDI) hand-carried ultrasound device capable of supporting medical operations in austere Role of Care (ROC) 3 environments with little to no modification. The selected vendor(s) will deliver two (2) prototype units for operational and environmental testing (MIL-STD-810H). The solution must be FDA cleared for human use, Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliant, and operate on standard CONUS/OCONUS power infrastructures. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(f), the Government advises all offerors that a noncompetitive follow-on production contract or transaction may be awarded to the participant(s) of this Prototype Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) without the use of competitive procedures Submission Instructions: Proposals must be submitted via DoD SAFE file transfer or secure email. Submit to: Timothy Compton, Agreements Officer (timothy.j.compton7.civ@army.mil) Copy to: Roxanne A. Dalrymple, Agreements Specialist (roxanne.a.dalrymple.civ@army.mil) Please see attached.

title: CFLHD Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) for Architect-Engineer Design Services
description: Architect and Engineering (A-E) Services The Federal Highway Administration, Central Federal Lands Highway Division (CFLHD), anticipates soliciting and awarding multiple Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for A-E services with a partial small business set-aside. CFLHD provides engineering and construction services on projects in the states of Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming on behalf of Federal Land Management Agencies and other Agencies. These Agencies include: the National Park Service (NPS); USDA Forest Service (Forest Service); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS); Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) and Tribal Governments; Bureau of Land Management (BLM); Department of Defense (DOD); U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE); and the Bureau of Reclamation (BOR). The shared capacity of the IDIQs will be $60 million. The acquisition will be solicited and awarded on a competitive basis and is being made under the North America Industry Classification Code 541330 and is open to all business concerns. The planned duration for the contracts is a total of five years. Projects are typically located in environmentally sensitive areas that necessitate context-sensitive design techniques and processes. Project topography type and climatic zones vary greatly including coastal, mountainous, desert and plains regions. Projects will primarily involve improvements to low-volume and low-speed roadways ranging from 3R (resurfacing, restoration and rehabilitation) to full reconstruction. The geographic jurisdiction of CFLHD includes, but is not limited to, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming.

title: USP Canaan IPS Supply and Startup
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP), USP Canaan, requires the furnishing and delivery of emergency lighting inverter systems and factory-authorized startup services. The Government shall perform installation under separate means. The Contractor shall not perform installation, demolition, wiring, removal of existing equipment, conduit work, or electrical construction. The products identified below are being procured on a Brand Name or Equal basis. Equal products must meet all salient characteristics contained in attached PWS for Myers Power Systems. To be considered for award, offers of 'equal' products must submit all descriptive literature and technical data necessary for the Contracting Officer to determine whether the product meets the salient characteristics specified in this solicitation. The submission must include the exact make, model, and manufacturer, alongside a cross-reference confirming compliance with each listed characteristic. Failure to provide sufficient technical evidence will result in the quote being determined technically unacceptable. Evaluation Factors Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quotation represents the Best Value to the Government. The Government will evaluate quotations based on the following factors: Technical Compliance- The degree to which the proposed equipment meets or exceeds the salient characteristics and technical requirements identified in this solicitation, including the adequacy and completeness of supporting technical documentation and compliance with the Brand Name or Equal requirements. Delivery Schedule-The offeror's ability to meet or improve upon the Government's required delivery schedule, including proposed lead times for equipment delivery and startup services. Price-The total evaluated price for all CLINs. Past Performance- The Government may consider an offeror's past performance in supplying and delivering products similar in scope and complexity to the requirements of this solicitation. Evaluation may include the offeror's history of meeting delivery commitments, providing complete and accurate shipments, responding to customer concerns, and overall performance associated with the delivery of comparable equipment. Technical Compliance, Delivery Schedule, and Price, Past Performance will be considered in determining the quotation that represents the Best Value to the Government. The Government may award to other than the lowest-priced offeror if the additional value associated with a higher-rated quotation warrants the additional cost. Any contractor interested in obtaining a contract award with the Federal Bureau of Prisons must be registered at https://www.sam.gov/. Faith-Based and Community-Based Organizations have the right to submit offers equally with other organizations for contracts for which they are eligible. All responsible sources are encouraged to submit a written offer which will be considered for award. The solicitation will be available on or after November 6, 2026, with a due date of November 20, 2026 4:00 p.m. EST The solicitation will be distributed solely through the SAM beta.gov web site https://beta.sam.gov/ Hard copies of the solicitation document will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. All future information about this acquisition, including solicitation amendments, will also be distributed solely through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. Offerors must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) and possess a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) at the time of quotation submission and throughout contract performance. To be eligible for award, an offeror must be identified in SAM as a small business concern under NAICS Code 335999. The Government will verify the offeror's SAM registration, UEI, size status, and exclusion records prior to award. Offerors shall include their UEI in their quotation and on any solicitation response forms submitted to the Government. Failure to maintain an active SAM registration, possess a valid UEI, or qualify as a small business concern under the applicable NAICS code may render the quotation ineligible for award. Pursuant to Wage Determination 2015-4257, the specialized technical services required for the emergency power system startup and commissioning have been mapped to the most applicable labor categories defined within the Department of Labor (DOL) SCA Directory of Occupations. Pursuant to the Service Contract Labor Standards (SCLS) statute, it has been determined that the official occupational classification for this procurement is Engineering Technician IV (Occupational Code 30084) Instructions to Offerors Offerors shall submit a completed Standard Form (SF) 1449, Solicitation/Contract/Order for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, with their quotation. All offerors shall submit their completed submission to both Chris Ficken, cficken@bop.gov and Joseph Kozuch, jkozuch@bop.gov. The offeror's Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) shall be entered in Block 17a of the SF 1449. The UEI provided on the SF 1449 must match the offeror's active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors shall include all technical documentation, product literature, warranty information, delivery lead times, and pricing necessary for the Government to evaluate the quotation. The Government will verify the apparent successful offeror's SAM registration, UEI, business size status, and eligibility for award prior to contract award. Failure to provide a completed SF 1449, including a valid UEI in Block 17a, may render a quotation ineligible for award.

title: Commercial Solution Opportunity - Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) CONUS
description: In accordance with the Commercial Solutions Opening � Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA), posted October 2, 2026, under Notice ID HQCAAA2701, the following requirement supports Area of Interest (AoI) 5.1 Accelerate Eligible Patron Growth. The parent CSO with instructions is located at Related ID HQCAAA2701. The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is seeking innovative, commercial approaches for a digital storefront, in-store fulfillment, and delivery solution(s), hereinafter referred to as �DeCA2U�. The primary goal of DeCA2U is to deliver a seamless, modern, and fully integrated omnichannel grocery experience for authorized patrons at Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) locations in the contiguous United States (CONUS), Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico that matches or exceeds the best commercial grocery services available today. The DeCA2U solution shall utilize a market-aligned commercial financial model typical of leading grocery retailers. The prospective contractor shall identify all locations in which it could provide an entire end-to-end solution enabling authorized patrons to place grocery orders, make payment, and receive their groceries at a designated delivery location. Specifically, DeCA2U will provide one unified, easy-to-use platform enabling authorized patrons and military units to: Shop and order groceries online anytime, anywhere via mobile app or website; Receive accurate real-time inventory and pricing from their local commissary; Benefit from fast, accurate in-store picking and professional order assembly; Enjoy reliable, tracked doorstep delivery directly to their home or quarters or convenient curbside pickup; Track and be rewarded for purchases; Leverage value-added functionality like forgotten items, �People who bought this� recommendations, menu building, price checking, or any other shopping experience enhancement capability; and Complete transactions through a secure, seamless payment process supporting all tender types including, but not limited to, MILITARY STAR and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT). The Government reserves the right to add payment options. Offerors shall propose pricing reflecting current commercial market rates for similar omnichannel. The Service Contract Labor Standards (formerly the Service Contract Act), 41 U.S.C. ��6701 et seq. will be applicable to any resulting contract. The desired outcome is to establish a long-term commercial partnership that provides authorized commissary patrons with a convenient, reliable, and cost-effective grocery shopping experience through an integrated solution for online ordering, payment processing, order fulfillment, pickup, and delivery. The solution should leverage proven commercial capabilities, support operational efficiency, enhance the commissary benefit, and provide a scalable and sustainable service model that can adapt to evolving mission requirements and patron needs. Proposed solutions should comply with applicable commercial and/or Department of War (DoW) cybersecurity standards, including but not limited to, SOC 2 Type 2. Additionally, integrated payment and entitlement gateways supporting all tender types including, but not limited to, MILITARY STAR and SNAP EBT. Proposed solutions must meet current commercial PCI DSS compliance and USDA Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) digital security specifications. The platform shall ensure robust end-to-end encryption for data at rest and in transit (FIPS 140-3 validated) and secure patron Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in accordance with federal privacy standards. Solutions shall propose a Period of Performance (PoP) that reflects customary commercial lead times, development lifecycles, and delivery benchmarks for the proposed capability. The Government reserves the right to adjust the proposed PoP to align with mission requirements, funding availability, and applicable regulatory limitations, including structuring the award as a base period with one or more option periods at the Government�s discretion. DeCA will not endorse any contractor employee for the purpose of installation access; as such, solutions shall address their proposed approach to meeting applicable military installation access requirements, including personnel screening, credentialing, and delivery access procedures. DeCA will utilize the phased evaluation process established in the overarching Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), Notice ID HQCAAA2701. Interested vendors with demonstrated commercial experience in grocery eCommerce, order fulfillment, pickup, delivery, or integrated retail solutions with foundational information security management system standard should submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief in accordance with the applicable submission requirements of the overarching CSO. Solution Briefs should describe: the proposed commercial approach; relevant capabilities; anticipated benefits to DeCA and its authorized patrons; proposed business model; PoP; Service Contract Labor Standards; installation access; and cybersecurity measures. Additionally, all proposed solutions shall address the vendor's ability to integrate with DeCA�s retail ecosystems and scale to DeCA�s business needs. The Government will evaluate submissions in accordance with the criteria established in the overarching CSO and may invite selected vendors to participate in subsequent phases. The closing date for this �Call for Solution� is Friday 13 November 2026 at 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). All communications, including solution brief information and submission requirements shall be sent via email to the following Points of Contact: Diana Gross-Bendall, email: diana.gross-bendall@deca.mil and Tinitia Gholson, email: tinitia.gholson@deca.mil.

title: CFLHD Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) for Architect-Engineer Design Services
description: Architect and Engineering (A-E) Services The Federal Highway Administration, Central Federal Lands Highway Division (CFLHD), anticipates soliciting and awarding multiple Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for A-E services with a partial small business set-aside. CFLHD provides engineering and construction services on projects in the states of Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming on behalf of Federal Land Management Agencies and other Agencies. These Agencies include: the National Park Service (NPS); USDA Forest Service (Forest Service); U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS); Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) and Tribal Governments; Bureau of Land Management (BLM); Department of Defense (DOD); U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE); and the Bureau of Reclamation (BOR). The shared capacity of the IDIQs will be $60 million. The acquisition will be solicited and awarded on a competitive basis and is being made under the North America Industry Classification Code 541330 and is open to all business concerns. The planned duration for the contracts is a total of five years. Projects are typically located in environmentally sensitive areas that necessitate context-sensitive design techniques and processes. Project topography type and climatic zones vary greatly including coastal, mountainous, desert and plains regions. Projects will primarily involve improvements to low-volume and low-speed roadways ranging from 3R (resurfacing, restoration and rehabilitation) to full reconstruction. The geographic jurisdiction of CFLHD includes, but is not limited to, Arizona, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Kansas, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming.

title: BST-1 Electrical Hull Penetrator and Transmitter Cable Assembly
description: This Sources Sought notice is being issued by the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD), on behalf of the NSWCPD Division 45. The Government is seeking information regarding the procurement of a maximum of twenty (20) Electrical Hull Penetrators (EHP). Specifications are listed in the attached Sources Sought Notice. SUBMISSION OF RESPONSES: Respondents shall provide capability statements with specific information regarding their ability to provide the required materials (described in the Sources Sought Attachment) to meet Division 45 needs. NSWCPD will only accept unclassified, electronic submissions. Responses shall be submitted via email to christopher.m.mccarthy26.civ@us.navy.mil by 16:30 EST, 20 November 2026. Responses shall list N64498-RFPREQ-PD-45-0176 in the subject line. No phone calls shall be accepted. Government WILL NOT PAY for any information received, and the Government will not compensate the respondent for any cost incurred in developing the response to this notice. The Government will not release any information marked with a proprietary legend received in response to this notice to any firms, agencies or individuals outside the Government without written permission in accordance with the legend. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. This is a follow up Sources Sought Notice to an Industry Day Virtual Event held on 27 October 2026. During that event the following questions were asked. Below each question is the answer to said question. Question #1: Is this 10/27 conference a virtual event via a web link or on site at Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD)? Answer #1: This event will take place on Microsoft TEAMs. You need to register on Eventbrite to access the link. Question #2: For this PRE-SOL for Columbia Class BST-1 Electrical Hull Penetrators and Transmitter Cable Assemblies, do cable assembly manufacturers need to have SUBSAFE Level 1 or 2 certification for doing hull penetrator work? Answer #2: The Electric Hull Penetrators (EHP) is Level I material within the SUBSAFE boundary and any vendor does not need to be in NAVSEA Note5000. Question #3: I looked again at the link and there are no answers or questions posted let alone a specific statement about SubSafe Level 1 or 2. It does mention � in accordance with applicable documents in Section 2.0 and the Statement of Work� but there is no such documents on the link. Answer #3: Again to Confirm, The Electric Hull Penetrators (EHP) is Level I material within the SUBSAFE boundary and any vendor does not need to be in NAVSEA Note5000. As for the Section 2.0 Documents and Statement of Work, those have not been provided to any vendors at this time. They will be provided at the time the official Request for Proposal (RFP) goes out. The anticipated date that the RFP goes out has not been determined yet. Question #4: We would request that the solicitation be issued as full and open given the NAICS code stated. Answer #4: Our team is still evaluating whether competing the contract as full and open or set aside is the best path forward. Question #5: Previously a vendor has been shown specifications for a cable used on BST-1 (BST-1 CABLE REQUIREMENTS PER 1197262 (PC 19). Is the cable still a 2SWF-2 (Modified) and if so, is a neoprene outer jacket still mandatory? Answer #5: The cable is still required to be LS2SWU-12 which includes a polyolefin outer jacket. Additionally, this cable will require exterior armor for EMI protection. Question #6: Question for you regarding Welding NDT. Do you need us to complete the Shipbuilder's LVL3 NDT? Answer #6: Personnel qualified to LVL 2 are permitted to perform the weld NDT, the NDT inspection must be approved by LVL 3 qualified personnel. Question #7: For the section where the pressure proof caps go on, are those welded to the main body and require a QQ-N-286 weld procedure? Does NSWC-PD need to certify this weld procedure? Answer #7: Yes, the 4 receptacles are welded to the main body. The weld type is monel QQ-N-281 to k-monel QQ-N-286. For additional guidance on performing the weld, please refer to the latest revision of NAVSEA Tech Publication 278. The procedure developed using the guidance in 278 requires NSWCPD approval. NSWCPD would be looking for the vendor to submit their weld procedure specification (WPS), product quality report (PQR), and welder qualifications for approval. Attached to this Sources Sought Notice are Two Documents: A Breakdown of the sources sought notice in a word document and what is being requested with this notice A distributable guidance that helps give newcomers an initial roadmap to preparing to support work producing Level I material. An updated slideshow from the Industry Day Event with the questions asked and said answers during and immediately after the event. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A TASK ORDER AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

title: AMS Designated Laboratory Meat Testing Services (ADL)
description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is issuing Solicitation 12?1NTS?26?R?0002 to obtain proposals from responsible, accredited analytical laboratories to perform microbiological and fat testing in support of AMS meat, poultry, egg, and aquatic product procurement programs. This requirement establishes AMS Designated Laboratories (ADLs) responsible for conducting all required microbiological and chemical analyses on samples submitted by AMS vendors, ensuring compliance with Federal Purchase Program Specifications (FPPS) and supporting food safety and quality verification efforts. AMS intends to award an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) firm?fixed?price contract, consisting of a Base Period and up to four option periods, covering performance from April 1, 2027 through March 31, 2032. Offerors must be fully capable of meeting all technical, accreditation, reporting, and quality assurance requirements outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW) and must maintain ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for all applicable microbiological and chemical test methods throughout the contract term. Offerors are required to submit a complete proposal package in accordance with Section E of the solicitation, including all technical, management, past performance, and pricing components, as well as a properly completed and signed SF?1449. Offerors must ensure all requirements, instructions, and submission details�such as WBSCM electronic submission processes�are fully reviewed and followed. Incomplete proposals may not be considered for award. Key expectations under this solicitation include: � Performance of all required microbiological and fat analyses using approved methods (FSIS MLG, AOAC, AOCS, or AMS?approved alternatives). � Comprehensive sample preparation, receipt, testing, reporting, and data management in accordance with AMS SOW requirements. � Timely reporting of results, including notification of presumptive or confirmed pathogen positives to AMS, FSIS, and vendors. � Secure handling and management of proprietary AMS data. � Full compliance with FAR, AGAR, and USDA?specific contract clauses incorporated into the solicitation. Prospective offerors are strongly encouraged to read the entire solicitation package, including the SOW, exhibits, and all referenced clauses, to ensure a complete and conforming submission.

Solicitation number 70Z03826RB0000006 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The United States Coast Guard (USCG), Aviation Logistics Center (ALC), Elizabeth City, NC intends to award an Indefinite Delivery Requirements type contract to BAE Systems Land & Armaments, L.P. (BAE) of Phoenix, AZ. This requirement will be solicited on an other than full and open competition basis under the authority of FAR 12.102 (b) for the procurement of spare parts for the pilot, co-pilot, and mechanic aircraft seats on the MH-65E Aircraft. BAE (Cage Code 54786) is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the only distributor source in North America capable of providing the required parts in the Schedule. The contract will consist of a one-year base period and if exercised, up to four (4) one-year option periods. This contract shall not exceed five (5) years. See the following attached documents titled: �Attachment 1 � Schedule of Supplies 70Z03826RB0000006�, �Attachment 2 � Provisions, Clauses, and Terms and Conditions 70Z03826RB0000006�, and �Attachment 3 - Redacted J and A � 70Z03826RB0000006�. Concerns having the expertise and required capabilities to provide these items are invited to submit offers in accordance with the requirements stipulated in this solicitation. Parts must be approved in accordance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) guidelines to ensure safety of our aircrew. The Government shall ensure all procurements are awarded without jeopardizing quality or safety of flight. Only the use of airworthy commercial specifications or standard military specifications/military standard parts will be utilized and approved from this solicitation. Newly manufactured commercial items will only be procured from sources able to provide a Certificate of Conformance (COC) and traceability to the OEM. The Federal Aviation Regulation, Part 21, outlines certification procedures. The contractor shall furnish a Certificate of Conformance (COC) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) clause 52.246-15. Certificate of conformance must be submitted in the format specified in the clause. All parts shall be NEW approved parts. Offerors must be able to provide necessary certification including traceability to the manufacturer, manufacturer's COC and its own COC to ensure parts are in airworthy condition, suitable for installation on USCG aircraft. Prospective vendors who are not the OEM or an authorized distributor must provide traceability for the offered product back to the manufacturer or authorized distributor. Traceability means a clear, complete, documented, and auditable paper trail which traces each step from an OEM or distributor to its current location. Traceability to the OEM must have only two exchanges prior to USCG delivery. Alternate parts will not be authorized. NO SUBSTITUTE PARTS WILL BE CONSIDERED. ONLY NEW PARTS WILL BE ACCEPTED. The Government reserves the right to withhold any item or group of items contained in this solicitation upon award. The Government reserves the right to make a single award, to make multiple awards covering different subsets of CLINs, or to make no award. The Government shall assume, for the purpose of making multiple awards, that $500 would be the administrative cost to the Government for issuing and administering each contract awarded under this solicitation. Individual awards shall be for the items or combinations of items that result in the lowest cost to the Government including the assumed administrative costs. The government shall ensure all procurements are awarded without jeopardizing quality or safety of flight. NOTE: NO DRAWINGS, SPECIFICATIONS OR SCHEMATICS ARE AVAILABLE FROM THIS AGENCY. description: Η παρούσα μελέτη αφορά την ανάδειξη αναδόχου / αναδόχων μελετητών για την εκπόνηση μελετών και την έκδοση των απαιτούμενων αδειών για την αποκατάσταση 3 ιδιόκτητων κτιρίων του e-ΕΦΚΑ και συγκεκριμένα των κτιρίων: 1. Επί της οδού Σοφοκλέους 39 στην Αθήνα, 2. Επί της οδού Πειραιώς 26 στην Αθήνα, 3. Επί των οδών Παπαστράτου 3 - 5, Δαφνίου 2 και Γραβιάς 2 στον Πειραιά. Επισημαίνεται ότι τα 2 πρώτα κτίρια είναι ήδη χαρακτηρισμένα ως διατηρητέα ενώ το 3ο κτίριο, παρότι δεν είναι επισήμως χαρακτηρισμένο ως διατηρητέο, κρίνεται ως εξαιρετικά πιθανός ο χαρακτηρισμός του, αφού η ηλικία του υπερβαίνει τα 100 έτη. Τα τρία αυτά κτίρια είναι σήμερα σε εξαιρετικά κακή κατάσταση και χαρακτηρίζονται ως επικίνδυνα. Έτσι, ο βασικός σκοπός της εκπόνησης των σχετικών μελετών είναι κατά κύριο λόγο η διάσωση των κτιρίων αυτών από την πλήρη κατάρρευση τα επόμενα χρόνια, με ότι αυτό συνεπάγεται για τον κίνδυνο ατυχήματος ή/και δυστυχήματος (παρότι έχουν ήδη ληφθεί μέτρα προφύλαξης (τοποθέτηση σκαφών / μεταλλικών κατασκευών) για την αποτροπή τους. Περαιτέρω όμως κρίνεται ότι, λόγω της θέσης τους, τα εν λόγω ακίνητα, όταν ανακατασκευαστούν, θα αποτελέσουν σημαντικά κτίρια προς αξιοποίηση (μέσω της εκμίσθωσής τους) και την προσδοκία σημαντικών εσόδων για τον e-ΕΦΚΑ από αυτά.

Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης είναι η ανάθεση της προμήθειας εξοπλισμού συστημάτων ασφαλείας με τις εργασίες εγκατάστασης του & υπηρεσίες ανάλυσης και αξιολόγησης κινδύνων σε Δημοτικά κτίρια (Δ/νση Παιδικών Σταθμών Άνω Λιοσίων, Κοινωνική Υπηρεσία-Άνω Λιοσια, Φιλαρμονική-Άνω Λιόσια, Κτηνιατρείο -Άνω Λιόσια, Αποθήκη υδραυλικών -Άνω Λιόσια, Τμήμα Πρασίνου-Εργατ. Κατοικίες Γεννηματά 2 Άνω Λιοσίων, Αντλιοστάσιο-Φυλή, Δημαρχείο Χασιάς -Φυλή) και σχολεία Πρωτοβάθμιας και Δευτεροβάθμιας Εκπαίδευσης του Δήμου Φυλής, στις τρεις Δημοτικές Ενότητες( Άνω Λιόσια, Ζεφύρι και Φυλή) με σκοπό την προστασία των κτιρίων από κινδύνους όπως η διάρρηξη, η κλοπή, η πυρκαγιά, καθώς και η απομακρυσμένη πρόσβαση σε μη εξουσιοδοτημένους χρήστες. Η ανάθεση της προμήθειας κρίνεται αναγκαία για την προστασία των δημοτικών κτιρίων αφενός και αφετέρου λόγω της ιδιαίτερης αύξησης των περιστατικών βανδαλισμού και κλοπών τα τελευταία έτη στα σχολεία του Δήμου, γεγονός που υποβαθμίζει την ασφάλεια, την ποιότητα των υπηρεσιών και την εύρυθμη λειτουργία των σχολικών μονάδων. Η συνολική δαπάνη προϋπολογίζεται να ανέλθει στις 273.420,00€ συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (Προϋπολογισμός χωρίς ΦΠΑ 220.500,00€ + ΦΠΑ 52.920,00€ = 273.420,00€). Στο ως άνω ποσό συμπεριλαμβάνεται και δικαίωμα προαίρεσης 50% προϋπολογισμού 91.140,00€ συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (Προϋπολογισμός προαίρεσης χωρίς ΦΠΑ 73.500,00€ + ΦΠΑ προαίρεσης 17.640,00€ = 91.140,00€). Ο προϋπολογισμός της σύμβασης χωρίς την προαίρεση προϋπολογίζεται να ανέλθει στις 182.280,00€ συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (Προϋπολογισμός χωρίς προαίρεση και ΦΠΑ 147.000,00€ + ΦΠΑ χωρίς προαίρεση 35.280,00€ = 182.280,00€). Η δαπάνη για την εν λόγω σύμβαση βαρύνει τις με Α.Λ.Ε.: - 030. 2420902001 για εργασίες και παροχή υπηρεσιών και - 030.3120989001 για προμήθεια εξοπλισμού σχετικές πιστώσεις του τακτικού προϋπολογισμού των οικονομικών ετών 2027-2028-2029 του Δήμου Φυλής, λαμβάνοντας ως δεδομένο ότι έχει ενεργοποιηθεί η προαίρεση και συγκεκριμένα: • 182.280,00€ συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% για τα έτη 2027 – 2028 [91.140,00€ για το οικονομικό έτος 2027 (34.100,00€ για εργασίες εγκατάστασης, 12.400,00€ για παροχή υπηρεσιών συμβουλών σε θέματα ασφάλειας και 44.640,00 για προμήθεια εξοπλισμού) και 91.140,00€ για το οικονομικό έτος 2028 (34.100,00€ για εργασίες εγκατάστασης, 12.400,00€ για παροχή υπηρεσιών συμβουλών σε θέματα ασφάλειας και 44.640,00 για προμήθεια εξοπλισμού)]. • 91.140,00€ συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% για το έτος 2029 [προαίρεση, εφόσον ενεργοποιηθεί (45.880,00€ για εργασίες εγκατάστασης και 45.260,00€ για προμήθεια εξοπλισμού)]. Οι εργασίες εγκατάστασης (CPV 45312000-7 : Εργασίες εγκατάστασης συστημάτων συναγερμού και κεραιών) αφορούν τα άρθρα 1,35 των αντίστοιχων πινάκων των τεχνικών προδιαγραφών και του ενδεικτικού προϋπολογισμού της υπ’ αριθμ. 93/2026 μελέτης της Τεχνικής Υπηρεσίας για τα δύο πρώτα έτη. Η παροχή υπηρεσιών (CPV 79417000-0 : Υπηρεσίες παροχής συμβουλών σε θέματα ασφάλειας) αφορά το άρθρο 37 και τα υπόλοιπα άρθρα (2-34 και 36) αφορούν προμήθεια εξοπλισμού ( CPV 35121700-5 : Συστήματα συναγερμού). Όσον αφορά την προαίρεση (εφόσον ενεργοποιηθεί), οι εργασίες εγκατάστασης αφορούν τα άρθρα 1,3 των αντίστοιχων πινάκων των τεχνικών προδιαγραφών και του ενδεικτικού προϋπολογισμού της μελέτης. Τα υπόλοιπα άρθρα (2 και 4-28) αφορούν προμήθεια εξοπλισμού. Οι ποσότητες των υλικών και εργασιών που αναφέρονται στον Πίνακα Ενδεικτικού Προϋπολογισμού της υπ’αιθμ.93/2026 μελέτης είναι ενδεικτικές και όχι δεσμευτικές για την αναθέτουσα αρχή. Ο Δήμος δεν είναι υποχρεωμένος να εξαντλήσει ολόκληρη την ποσότητα των ειδών της προμήθειας και των εργασιών και το αντίστοιχο εγκεκριμένο ποσό, εφόσον οι ανάγκες του αποδειχθούν μικρότερες κατά την εκτέλεση της υπογραφείσας σύμβασης. Η ποσότητα όμως που θα παραλαμβάνεται δεν μπορεί να είναι μικρότερη από το 50% της συνολικής, που προβλέπεται από τον εγκεκριμένο προϋπολογισμό. Οι ποσότητες των ειδών προμήθειας και των εργασιών είναι ενδεικτικές. Θα μπορούν να αυξομειωθούν ανάλογα με τις ανάγκες της Υπηρεσίας που θα χειριστεί την προς εκτέλεση προμήθεια, κατόπιν σχετικής ειδοποίησης. Οι τυχόν αλλαγές δεν θα υπερβαίνουν το ποσό της δαπάνης της σύμβασης. Ο ανάδοχος δεν διατηρεί καμία αξίωση για αποζημίωση ή διαφυγόντα κέρδη σε περίπτωση που η απορρόφηση υπολείπεται του αρχικού ενδεικτικού προϋπολογισμού και πάντως είναι μεγαλύτερη από το 50% αυτού. Η προμήθεια κατατάσσεται στους Κωδικούς Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων - 35121700-5 : Συστήματα συναγερμού - 45312000-7 : Εργασίες εγκατάστασης συστημάτων συναγερμού και κεραιών - 79417000-0 : Υπηρεσίες παροχής συμβουλών σε θέματα ασφάλειας Η εκτέλεση της παραπάνω προμήθειας θα γίνει με την διενέργεια δημόσιου ηλεκτρονικού διαγωνισμού άνω των ορίων και με κριτήριο κατακύρωσης την πλέον συμφέρουσα από οικονομική άποψη προσφοράς, βάσει τιμής ως μεικτή σύμβαση με βασικό χαρακτήρα την προμήθεια, σύμφωνα με τις διατάξεις του Ν.4412/2016 όπως τροποποιήθηκαν και ισχύουν, για το σύνολο των προς προμήθεια ειδών και των προς εκτέλεση εργασιών και υπηρεσιών. Η παρούσα προμήθεια δεν υποδιαιρείται σε τμήματα. Προσφορές υποβάλλονται για το σύνολο των ειδών, εργασιών και υπηρεσιών Η διάρκεια υλοποίησης της προμήθειας ορίζεται σε δύο (2) έτη, αρχόμενης από την υπογραφή της σύμβασης, χωρίς να ασκηθεί το δικαίωμα προαίρεσης και τρία (3) έτη εφόσον ασκηθεί

title: Greece – Provider services – «Παροχή Υπηρεσιών Δημόσιου Υπολογιστικού Νέφους & Υποστήριξης για το Ενιαίο Κυβερνητικό Νέφος»
description: Η παρούσα σύμβαση αφορά στη συνέχιση για δύο (2) επιπλέον έτη και στην επεκτασιμότητα υφιστάμενων νεφοϋπολογιστικών υποδομών Δημόσιου Υπολογιστικού Νέφους, οι οποίες έχουν ήδη υλοποιηθεί και λειτουργούν επιχειρησιακά στο πλαίσιο του κυβερνητικού υβριδικού περιβάλλοντος, αξιοποιώντας την πλατφόρμας Microsoft Azure. Η συνέχιση αυτή στοχεύει στη διασφάλιση της απρόσκοπτης λειτουργίας, της επεκτασιμότητας και της επιχειρησιακής ετοιμότητας των υπολογιστικών και δικτυακών υποδομών που υποστηρίζουν τα κυβερνητικά νέφη G-Cloud και H-Cloud, σύμφωνα με τις απαιτήσεις της Ψηφιακής Βίβλου και του Νόμου 4727/2020. Στο πλαίσιο αυτό, η συνέχιση της παροχής υπηρεσιών επιτρέπει την κάλυψη των αναγκών της Δημόσιας Διοίκησης για κεντρικές νεφοϋπολογιστικές υποδομές, οι οποίες υποστηρίζουν κρίσιμες ψηφιακές υπηρεσίες και πληροφοριακά συστήματα υψηλών απαιτήσεων σε διαθεσιμότητα, απόδοση και ασφάλεια. Οι εν λόγω τεχνολογικές υποδομές αποτελούν βασική προϋπόθεση για την περαιτέρω ωρίμανση και εμβάθυνση του ψηφιακού μετασχηματισμού της Δημόσιας Διοίκησης και συμβάλλουν καθοριστικά στη βελτίωση της αποδοτικότητας των δημόσιων υπηρεσιών και στην υποστήριξη της ψηφιακής οικονομίας. Το προς υλοποίηση έργο αφορά στη συνέχιση της κάλυψης των αναγκών της Δημόσιας Διοίκησης σε κεντρικές νεφοϋπολογιστικές υποδομές, οι οποίες χρησιμοποιούνται ευρέως για την υποστήριξη κρίσιμων επιχειρησιακών και πληροφοριακών υπηρεσιών και συστημάτων. Το έργο διασφαλίζει τη συνεχιζόμενη λειτουργία, διαθεσιμότητα και επεκτασιμότητα των σχετικών υποδομών και περιλαμβάνει ενδεικτικά τις ακόλουθες κατηγορίες υπηρεσιών: 1. Υπηρεσίες φιλοξενίας παρόχου Δημόσιου Υπολογιστικού Νέφους της πλατφόρμας Microsoft Azure 2. Υπηρεσίες υποστήριξης παρόχου Δημόσιου Υπολογιστικού Νέφους που αφορούν στη συνέχιση της ολοκληρωμένης τεχνικής υποστήριξης που παρέχεται απευθείας από τον πάροχο του Δημόσιου Υπολογιστικού Νέφους, μέσω της υπηρεσίας Microsoft Unified Enterprise Support, εξασφαλίζοντας την απρόσκοπτη λειτουργία των υφιστάμενων πληροφοριακών συστημάτων και την άμεση διαχείριση κρίσιμων περιστατικών κατά το χρονικό διάστημα της σύμβασης. 3. Υπηρεσίες αναδόχου Μετάπτωσης, Ανάπτυξης Συστημάτων και Δεδομένων στο Δημόσιο Υπολογιστικό Νέφος που καλύπτουν τόσο τη μετάπτωση όσο και την ανάπτυξη εφαρμογών και των αντίστοιχων δεδομένων τους στο Δημόσιο Υπολογιστικό Νέφος. Ειδικότερα, οι υπηρεσίες μετάπτωσης αφορούν αποκλειστικά τη μεταφορά των υποδομών και των συστημάτων που φιλοξενούν τις εφαρμογές και τα δεδομένα τους, χωρίς να περιλαμβάνουν ενέργειες που σχετίζονται με την προσαρμογή, ανασχεδίαση ή επανανάπτυξη των ίδιων των εφαρμογών στο νέο περιβάλλον. Οι εν λόγω ενέργειες εμπίπτουν στην αρμοδιότητα του φορέα που αιτείται τη παροχή των υπηρεσιών μετάπτωσης στην αναθέτουσα αρχή και δεν αποτελούν μέρος του παρόντος αντικειμένου. 4. Υπηρεσίες αναδόχου συνολικής διακυβέρνησης Ψηφιακού Χαρτοφυλακίου στο Δημόσιο Υπολογιστικό Νέφος που αφορούν στη συνέχιση της ολιστικής διακυβέρνησης, εποπτείας και διαχείρισης των πόρων, υπηρεσιών και εφαρμογών που λειτουργούν στο Δημόσιο Υπολογιστικό Νέφος, σύμφωνα με το υφιστάμενο λειτουργικό και τεχνολογικό πλαίσιο. Στόχος είναι η διατήρηση της επιχειρησιακής συνέχειας, της ασφάλειας και της βέλτιστης οικονομικής διαχείρισης για την επόμενη διετία. 5. Υπηρεσίες υποστήριξης αναδόχου (Helpdesk) Υποδομών IaaS, Υπηρεσιών PaaS και Διαχειριστικών Λύσεων στο Δημόσιο Υπολογιστικό Νέφος που αφορούν στη συνεχιζόμενη επίλυση προβλημάτων και τεχνικών περιστατικών που σχετίζονται με τις νεφοϋπολογιστικές υποδομές, με σκοπό τη διατήρηση της ομαλής λειτουργίας τους κατά τη διάρκεια της σύμβασης. Οι υπηρεσίες υποστήριξης θα συνεχίσουν να παρέχονται σύμφωνα με τα ισχύοντα Service Level Agreements (SLA), όπως αναλυτικά περιγράφονται. 6. Λοιπές υπηρεσίες Στο πλαίσιο του έργου προβλέπεται επίσης, η παροχή και θέση σε λειτουργία νέων κυκλωμάτων διασύνδεσης μέσω ExpressRoute, για την ενίσχυση της δικτυακής συνδεσιμότητας των Φορέων με το Δημόσιο Υπολογιστικό Νέφος. Ειδικότερα, για τη ΓΓΠΣΨΔ προβλέπεται η εγκατάσταση και λειτουργία δύο (2) κυκλωμάτων χωρητικότητας 2 Gbps έκαστο (2+2 Gbps) για τη διασύνδεση της Αττικής με το Άμστερνταμ, ενώ για την ΗΔΥΚΑ προβλέπεται η εγκατάσταση και λειτουργία δύο (2) κυκλωμάτων χωρητικότητας 5 Gbps έκαστο (5+5 Gbps), σε διάταξη active-active, για τη διασύνδεση με τη Φρανκφούρτη. Τα κυκλώματα θα παρέχονται ως υπηρεσία και θα περιλαμβάνουν το σύνολο των απαιτούμενων ενεργειών για την εγκατάσταση, παραμετροποίηση, ενεργοποίηση, διασύνδεση και θέση τους σε παραγωγική λειτουργία, σύμφωνα με τις απαιτήσεις και τις τεχνικές προδιαγραφές του έργου. [παρ. 1.3 & ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ I της Διακήρυξης]

title: U.S. Navy and Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) MQ-4C Triton Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Sustaining Engineering and Support (SES) V Contract
description: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. The Naval Air Systems Command, PMA-262 (Program Office for MQ-4C Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS)), is soliciting information from industry to determine potential contractors who have the skills, experience, qualifications, and knowledge to provide the comprehensive engineering, logistics, material, maintenance, program management, and operational support required to successfully provide the sustaining and reach back engineering support needed to sustain the United States Navy and Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) MQ-4C Triton UAS at both Contiguous United States (CONUS) and Outside the Contiguous United States (OCONUS) locations. This effort includes up to higher than Secret classification level of support. Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation (NGSC) is the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of the MQ-4C Triton UAS. As such they possess the requisite technical data and knowledge to meet the Navy�s requirements for sustaining engineering support of the MQ-4C UAS. The contractor shall be responsible for obtaining from NGSC all manufacturing drawing and proprietary specification data necessary to support the sustainment of the MQ-4C Triton UAS. DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), BUT RATHER A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify interested sources capable of meeting the requirements. This RFI is issued solely for market research, planning and information purposes and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contractual agreement, nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. There is no commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation, make an award, or be responsible for any monies expended by any interested parties in support of the effort mentioned above. Vendors can additionally provide a capabilities statement of no more than five (5) pages in length that demonstrates the respondent�s ability to meet the requirements as specified herein. The Government is interested in receiving vendors� commercial published price lists for items they believe meet the need in this RFI. All data received in response to this RFI, marked or designated as corporate or proprietary, will be fully protected from release outside the Government. Failure to respond to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future associated RFP that may be issued. Information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit or award a contract. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the System for Award Management (SAM) website: www.sam.gov. It is the potential offeror�s responsibility to monitor this site for the release of any follow-on information. Interested parties are requested to submit a capability statement of no more than five (5) pages in length, demonstrating their ability to provide the specified services. The capability statement should include, at a minimum, the following: Company Name, Company Address, Company Business Size, CAGE code, and Point of Contact (POC) information to include POC�s name, phone number and email address. A detailed description of the company's experience in providing the required sustainment engineering services of a military UAS in CONUS and OCONUS locations. Evidence of access to the required technical data and specifications required to support the MQ-4C UAS. A description of the company's quality assurance processes and certifications. Any other relevant information that demonstrates the company's ability to meet the Government's requirements. Responses shall be submitted electronically to the designated Contract Specialist, Lara Chubb, in Microsoft Word format or Portable Document Format (PDF) at the following email address: lara.i.chubb.civ@us.navy.mil (or DOD Safe for larger files). All responses, including capability statements, shall be submitted no later than 5:00 PM EST, 20 November 2026. Questions or comments regarding this notice may be addressed to the Procuring Contracting Officer, Mr. Tyler Summers and Contract Specialist, Ms. Lara Chubb.

description: The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Port Hueneme Division (NSWC PHD) hereby gives notice of intent to sole source to AdvantEdge Technologies Inc. (ATI) (Cage Code 3PQL7) for a follow-on requirement for Self Defense Test Ship (SDTS) engineering and technical support services. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 541330 - Engineering Services, with a size standard of $ 47.0 million. This is a follow-on requirement for the continued provision of highly specialized services for operation, maintenance and repair of the current SDTS platform (Ex Paul F Foster, EDD 964). The SDTS Program consists of both the SDTS and Test Ship Remote Control System (TSRCS). The TSRCS provides the remote capability for the SDTS to operate in an unmanned capacity at sea in support of high-risk live-fire Test and Evaluation (T&E) events. The SDTS primarily supports T&E initiatives related to Engineering and Combat Systems (CS), Ship Self Defense System (SSDS), and various weapons, control, and engineering systems as needed by the Department of Defense (DoD) and Department of the Navy (DoN). The government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Awarding the follow-on SDTS support contract to any source other than ATI would introduce a transition period which would cause unacceptable mission delays to scheduled critical milestones and deployment timelines. The anticipated period of performance is three (3) years, inclusive of a base year and two (2) option years, covering the current SDTS platform�s end-of-life phase. All responsible sources may identify their interest and provide capability statements in response to this notice. Interested companies should submit, on company letterhead, a notice of interest including the name, telephone number, mailing address, and e-mail address of one point of contact. Responses to this notice should not exceed 10 pages (8.5 x 11 inch) and 12-point font Times New Roman font. Submission shall be in Microsoft Word or Adobe Acrobat and shall be sent electronically to the contract specialist at melissa.a.hautman.civ@us.navy.mil and the contracting officer at gary.l.heagy.civ@us.navy.mil. This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals. However, all responses received within 15 days of publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely at the discretion of the Government. DISCLAIMER: THIS SYNOPSIS IS FOR INFOMRATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL NOR DOES IT CONSITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS SYNOPSIS IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

description: This Special Notice is not a formal Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ) nor any type of Solicitation for offers. In accordance with FAR 15.201(d), this Special Notice is intended FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY in order to publicize the requirements of the Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research (FNLCR). The FNLCR is a Government-Owned Contractor-Operated Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC) located at Fort Detrick, Maryland. The FNLCR partners with university, Government, and corporate scientists to speed the translation of laboratory research into new diagnostic tests and treatments for cancer and AIDS. FNLCR is a multi-program laboratory currently operated by Leidos Biomedical Research, Inc. (Leidos Biomed) for the National Cancer Institute (NCI) under Prime Contract No. 75N91019D00024 & HHSN261201500003I, which provides Operations and Technical Support (OTS) for the FNLCR. The Government assumes no liability for reimbursement for any effort or associated costs to respond, nor for any information provided as a result of this Special Notice as no information is being requested. Please be advised that any submissions provided, despite that no information is requested, become Government property and will not be returned, nor will there be any ensuing discussions or debriefings. Responses submitted to this Special Notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site and any sites referenced herein for additional information pertaining to business opportunities with the FNLCR, if any. Description of Work: In response to the 2018 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the National Institutes of Health, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and Leidos Biomed Research, Inc. (Leidos Biomed) established a multilateral clinical research program called Pamoja Tulinde Maisha (PALM), meaning �Together Save Lives� in the Kiswahili language. This program was founded in partnership with the DRC�s National Institute of Biomedical Research (�Institut National de Recherche Biom�dicale� in French). The components of the PALM research program include: Research Platform: Subcontractor shall provide the core clinical infrastructure and services needed to conduct human subjects� research. Leidos Biomed has supported NIAID to initiate and sustain clinical research infrastructure across several research sites, laboratories, biorepository, pharmacy cold chain, data management operations, supply chain depots, and administrative/operations offices. Biorepository: Subcontractor shall provide support for the processing, tracking, storage, and transfer of biospecimens collected during PALM clinical research as well as storage and tracking of outbreak samples. Subcontractor shall provide support for clinical research protocols: PALM 004, an immunologic sub-study titled �Characterizing the immune responses to Bundibugyo virus disease and their associations with clinical outcomes� at four treatment centers in the outbreak region of Eastern DRC and one research site for recruitment of healthy volunteers in Kinshasa, DRC PALM 011, an observational cohort study of patients treated for mpox virus disease at two rural hospital sites in the DRC Leidos Biomedical Research, Inc. Point of Contact: If you are interested in obtaining the solicitation, please contact Heather Sewell, Lead Subcontracts Administrator at heather.sewell@nih.gov by 5:00 PM ET Friday, November 20, 2026.

title: W9123627BA004: NASA Wallops Breakwater Project in Wallops Island, Virginia
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice. This is NOT a solicitation. Do NOT submit proposals or questions in response to this notice. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be posted on Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website at https://piee.eb.mil/ by the end of November 2026. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted for 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Norfolk District (NAO) intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) acquisition for the NASA Wallops Shoreline Breakwaters Project in Accomack County, Virginia. This procurement will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 14, Invitation for Bid (IFB). The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract. The requirement will be solicited as a 100% small business set aside. The applicable NAICS code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction (Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities), with a small business standard of $45 million. In accordance with DFARS 236.204 - Disclosure of the Magnitude of Construction Projects, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. DESCRIPTION OF WORK The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers � Norfolk District is seeking eligible firms capable of constructing breakwaters along the beach of Wallops Island. The number of proposed breakwaters for this project will be between two to four and placed approximately 200 feet offshore (from Mean High Water elevation). Each breakwater will be constructed of Type II rip rap for armor stone and VDOT Class III stone for core stone. The weight of material for each breakwater is approximately 10,000 tons. Breakwaters are to be placed on 12-inch-thick marine mattress with geotextile fabric. Water depths for breakwater placement range between -9.5 ft and -12.0 ft NAVD88. Each breakwater will be constructed to a crest height of +7 ft NAVD88. Material for breakwaters may be transported to the project site either by land or sea. Construction of breakwaters may occur either by land or sea. Various work restrictions are expected due to active rocket launches within the vicinity of the project site, which will require all construction activities to stop and personnel to vacate the premises for hours to day(s). The construction completion date will be approximately 325 calendar days from the issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractors will be required to submit bid bonds documents with the proposal. The successful awardee will be required to provide 100% payment and performance bonds for the project. The effort will be solicited and awarded utilizing the Sealed Bid procedures under FAR Part 14. Anticipated solicitation issuance time frame is on or about the end of November 2026. THIS PROJECT IS A 100% SMALL BUSINESS SET ASIDE PROCUREMENT INVITATION FOR SEALED BID. The Government intends to award a firm fixed price contract using INVITATION FOR BID WITH PRE-AWARD SURVEY and procedures outlined in FAR 36 and FAR 14. Pre-award survey will determine contractor responsibility in accordance with FAR 9.104. Bidders will be evaluated on both pre-award survey and conformance to the solicitation and price. The Government reserves the right to reject any or all Bids; and to award the contract to other than the lowest total price and to award to the bidder submitting the lowest bid determined by the Government to be responsible. Bid bonds will be required with bid submittals. In addition, the awardee must be found responsible in accordance with FAR 9.1. The below Pre-Award Survey Information will be requested of the apparent low offeror. This information is not required to be responsive to the Invitation for Bid. a) Current commitments and expected dates of completion. b) One (1) signed bank reference demonstrating adequate financial resources. If bidder�s firm has a line of credit � provide information on how many figures bidder can borrow against the line of credit (i.e. medium 6 figures � exact line of credit is not required). c) The bidder shall provide the latest three (3) complete fiscal year financial statements for the prime contractor, certified by an independent accounting firm, if practicable, or signed by an authorized officer of the organization. Submit evidence of availability of working/operating capital, which will be used for the performance of the resultant contract. For Joint Venture arrangements, submit the latest three complete fiscal year financial statements for each company in the Joint Venture and discuss the financial responsibilities among the companies. The Government may also utilize Dun & Bradstreet reports to evaluate the financial capacity of the bidder. Definitive Responsibility Crieteria: This requirement will use Definitive Responsibility Criteria (DRC) which are specific and objective standards established to inform the Contracting Officer. In accordance with FAR 9.104-2. These criteria will be used to assess whether the apparent low bidder can demonstrate the expertise and specialized facilities needed for adequate contract performance. The inability of a contractor otherwise eligible for award to demonstrate minimally acceptable experience as measured by the DRC may result in the Contracting Officer determining the contractor is not responsible. The Definitive Responsibility Criteria will assess the following work items: 1. The apparent low bidder shall provide one documented experience of underwaterplacing at least 5,000 square yards of geotextile fabric or marine mattresses within the last 7 years. 2. The apparent low bidder shall provide documented experience proving successfully built at least one marine stone structure of at least 15,000 tons within the last 7 years. This notice does not constitute an invitation for bid. The IFB and accompanying documents will be issued electronically and will be uploaded to the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website at https://piee.eb.mil/ on or about the end of November 2026. Notification of any changes to this pre-solicitation will only be made on this website. Therefore, it is the offerors responsibility to check the website regularly for any posted changes to the pre-solicitation notice, release of the solicitation, specification, drawings, and all subsequent amendments. Telephone calls or written requests for the IFB package will NOT be accepted. Prospective bidders are responsible for monitoring at https://piee.eb.mil/ to respond to the solicitation and any amendments or other information regarding this acquisition. IT IS THE SOLE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE OFFEROR TO CONTINUALLY VIEW THE WEBSITE FOR CHANGES. No hard copies will be available. Prospective bidders are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov to respond to the solicitation and any amendments or other information regarding this acquisition. Prospective bidders are required to be registered in SAM when submitting an offer and shall continue to be registered until time of award, during performance, and through final payment of any contract. NOTE: Online Representations and Certifications Applications apply to this solicitation. Inquires must be directed to ProjNet in accordance with the forthcoming Solicitation document.

title: Request for Information--Gunshot-Related Threat Detection
description: Purpose This is a Request for Information (RFI). The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) is conducting market research to identify and evaluate innovative, stand-alone gunshot detection technologies suitable for an Interagency Security Committee (ISC) Level V facility. The objective of this RFI is to identify solutions that may enhance facility protection, improve threat detection, and support efficient security operations. Technologies submitted in response to this RFI must be authorized for Department of Homeland Security (DHS) use, operate independently of privacy-sensitive systems, and present no privacy concerns, including the collection, retention, or processing of personally identifiable information (PII). Scope FEMA seeks vendor capability statements and responses to the "Minimum Requirements" and "Requested Information" below as it relates to security technologies designed to detect and alert personnel to gunshot-related threats within or near an ISC Level V facility. Technologies of interest may include, but are not limited to, stand-alone acoustic, sensor-based, or other non-privacy-invasive gunshot detection solutions. Minimum Requirements Interested vendors should demonstrate that their solution meets the following requirements: Is authorized for DHS use, or can provide documentation supporting its DHS authorization status. Operates as a stand-alone solution and does not require integration with privacy-sensitive systems. Does not collect, retain, process, or transmit PII or other privacy-sensitive information. Provides capabilities relevant to gunshot detection and threat response in an ISC Level V facility environment. Supports timely alerting, situational awareness, and operational response. Can be presented through a vendor briefing and, if available, a live or virtual demonstration. Requested Information Vendors responding to this RFI should submit a capability statement that includes: Product name, description, and technical specifications. Overview of the solution�s gunshot detection and threat-mitigation capabilities. Description of how the solution operates as a stand-alone system. Explanation of privacy protections, including confirmation that the solution does not collect or process PII. Relevant use cases or prior deployments in ISC Level V facilities or comparable high-security environments. DHS authorization status and supporting documentation, as applicable. Availability for a vendor briefing and/or live demonstration. Primary point of contact, including name, title, organization, email address, and telephone number. Submission Deadline Interested vendors should submit responses no later than 5PM ET on 11/20/2026. If your response is selected for further review, you may be asked to provide a briefing and, when feasible, a live demonstration of capability.

Purpose The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Aviation (PAE(A)) Autonomy & Super Intelligence (SI) / Artificial Intelligence (AI) leadership team invites leaders, technical experts, and developers from Government, industry, and academia to participate in an upcoming Industry Day focused on autonomy and super intelligence/artificial intelligence mission areas relevant to Naval Aviation. The objectives of this event are to: Align Government, industry, and academic capabilities with Naval Aviation requirements. Identify technical, operational, and mission capability gaps. Increase awareness of commercial and academic tools relevant to current Navy development priorities. Inform potential future acquisition approaches to support near-term warfighter needs. III. title: Market Intelligence Notice � Child Development Centers (CDC) - Volumetric modular housing, Kit-of-Parts facilities, 3-D Printed
description: Market Intelligence Notice � Child Development Centers (CDC) - Volumetric modular housing, Kit-of-Parts facilities, 3-D Printed Disclaimer: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or a commitment to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. 1.0 Objective The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Savannah District (SAS) is seeking market intelligence to identify and assess industry capabilities relevant to Volumetric modular housing, Kit-of-Parts facilities, 3-D Printed and hybrid industrialized construction solutions for child development centers located on multiple military installations. The Government is pursuing modern industrialized construction approaches intended to improve schedule, cost, and lifecycle outcomes for this facility type. For purposes of this RFI, respondents should clearly identify whether they view these features as: Fully compatible with their standard commercial or industrialized building system; Achievable with modifications; or Better addressed through an alternative technical solution that provides equal or better performance. Where respondents recommend alternatives, the response should explain how the proposed approach would satisfy or improve upon the Government's desired performance outcomes for schedule; cost; capacity/readiness; child safety and program functionality; quality and durability; energy consumption; repeatability/scalability; site and installation impact; and compliance/turnover. Information provided by respondents will be used to help the Government understand available market participants, solution types, and industry interest, and will inform future industry engagements, acquisition planning, and assessment of potential use of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, Facility Construction or Repair: Transactions Other Than Contracts and Grants. 2.0 Forecasted Project(s) Overview The following projects are currently projected for potential industrialized construction applications. The work will be performed on multiple military installations. Solutions may be scaled for additional facilities identified later. Work will also include installation of video monitoring, alarm, and intercom systems for safety. title: W9123627BA004: NASA Wallops Breakwater Project in Wallops Island, Virginia
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice. This is NOT a solicitation. Do NOT submit proposals or questions in response to this notice. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be posted on Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website at https://piee.eb.mil/ by the end of November 2026. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted for 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Norfolk District (NAO) intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) acquisition for the NASA Wallops Shoreline Breakwaters Project in Accomack County, Virginia. This procurement will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 14, Invitation for Bid (IFB). The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract. The requirement will be solicited as a 100% small business set aside. The applicable NAICS code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction (Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities), with a small business standard of $45 million. In accordance with DFARS 236.204 - Disclosure of the Magnitude of Construction Projects, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. DESCRIPTION OF WORK The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers � Norfolk District is seeking eligible firms capable of constructing breakwaters along the beach of Wallops Island. The number of proposed breakwaters for this project will be between two to four and placed approximately 200 feet offshore (from Mean High Water elevation). Each breakwater will be constructed of Type II rip rap for armor stone and VDOT Class III stone for core stone. The weight of material for each breakwater is approximately 10,000 tons. Breakwaters are to be placed on 12-inch-thick marine mattress with geotextile fabric. Water depths for breakwater placement range between -9.5 ft and -12.0 ft NAVD88. Each breakwater will be constructed to a crest height of +7 ft NAVD88. Material for breakwaters may be transported to the project site either by land or sea. Construction of breakwaters may occur either by land or sea. Various work restrictions are expected due to active rocket launches within the vicinity of the project site, which will require all construction activities to stop and personnel to vacate the premises for hours to day(s). The construction completion date will be approximately 325 calendar days from the issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractors will be required to submit bid bonds documents with the proposal. The successful awardee will be required to provide 100% payment and performance bonds for the project. The effort will be solicited and awarded utilizing the Sealed Bid procedures under FAR Part 14. Anticipated solicitation issuance time frame is on or about the end of November 2026. THIS PROJECT IS A 100% SMALL BUSINESS SET ASIDE PROCUREMENT INVITATION FOR SEALED BID. The Government intends to award a firm fixed price contract using INVITATION FOR BID WITH PRE-AWARD SURVEY and procedures outlined in FAR 36 and FAR 14. Pre-award survey will determine contractor responsibility in accordance with FAR 9.104. Bidders will be evaluated on both pre-award survey and conformance to the solicitation and price. The Government reserves the right to reject any or all Bids; and to award the contract to other than the lowest total price and to award to the bidder submitting the lowest bid determined by the Government to be responsible. Bid bonds will be required with bid submittals. In addition, the awardee must be found responsible in accordance with FAR 9.1. The below Pre-Award Survey Information will be requested of the apparent low offeror. If bidder�s firm has a line of credit � provide information on how many figures bidder can borrow against the line of credit (i.e. medium 6 figures � exact line of credit is not required). c) The bidder shall provide the latest three (3) complete fiscal year financial statements for the prime contractor, certified by an independent accounting firm, if practicable, or signed by an authorized officer of the organization. Submit evidence of availability of working/operating capital, which will be used for the performance of the resultant contract. For Joint Venture arrangements, submit the latest three complete fiscal year financial statements for each company in the Joint Venture and discuss the financial responsibilities among the companies. The Government may also utilize Dun & Bradstreet reports to evaluate the financial capacity of the bidder. This notice does not constitute an invitation for bid. The IFB and accompanying documents will be issued electronically and will be uploaded to the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website at https://piee.eb.mil/ on or about the end of November 2026. Notification of any changes to this pre-solicitation will only be made on this website. Prospective bidders are responsible for monitoring at https://piee.eb.mil/ to respond to the solicitation and any amendments or other information regarding this acquisition. IT IS THE SOLE RESPONSIBILITY OF THE OFFEROR TO CONTINUALLY VIEW THE WEBSITE FOR CHANGES. No hard copies will be available. title: Space Power and Reactor Capabilities (SPARC) - Sources Sought Notice
description: NASA intends to issue the Space Power and Reactor Capabilities (SPARC) Final Request for Proposals (RFP) via sam.gov on or around November 20, 2026. A Sources Sought Notice for SPARC was posted to sam.gov on August 3, 2026, entitled "Space Power and Reactor Capabilities (SPARC) - Sources Sought Notice" and under Notice ID 80GRC026SPARC. A Draft RFP for SPARC was posted to sam.gov on August 30, 2026, entitled " Space Power and Reactor Capabilities (SPARC) - Draft Request for Proposals (DRFP)" and under Notice ID 80GRC026R0009. Interested parties are highly encouraged to review the Draft RFP posting for information regarding the acquisition including the Industry Day Presentation and Questions and Answers. The Notice ID for the SPARC Final RFP is likely be updated due to it being released in Government Fiscal Year (GFY) 2027. SPARC will be competed as a Multiple-Award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (MAIDIQ) contract to provide for the design, development, analysis, fabrication, assembly, verification, validation, test, evaluation, certification, delivery (ground and/or space), and sustaining maintenance and operations of space nuclear systems, subsystems, hardware, materials, and software. Specifically, SPARC is intended to be NASA's preferred contractual mechanism for the competition and award of task orders related to the Design, Deveopment, Test, and Evaluation (DDT&E) of the Lunar Reactor - 1 (LR-1) system. Concurrent with (and as part of) the competition and award of SPARC, NASA intends to compete the first task order to be awarded under SPARC in the LR-1 Phase 1 Task Order. This task order represents the first step in the development of LR-1 and provides for the following objectives: Objective 1. Develop a Preliminary Design Review (PDR) level design for LR-1 that achieves the defined requirements and ensures the technology readiness is sufficient to proceed to flight system development. Objective 2. Perform an electrically-heated integrated system test in a relevant environment (as defined by the requirements) that incorporates representative versions of the key subsystems (an engineering test unit (ETU)). Objective 3. Perform component-level radiation exposure testing to demonstrate the LR-1 design will operate as intended within the induced (reactor) and natural (Lunar surface) radiation environments.

Utilize a varied selection of blood culture bottle configurations (low volume samples; antimicrobial agent removal resins) and formulations capable of maximizing growth potential of various microorganisms (e.g. aerobic and anaerobic bacteria, fungi, and mycobacteria) shall be available. Have the capability to flag and alert the end-user of positive culture vials by simultaneous visual alert, sound alert and remote alert using existing software programs. The Sheridan VAMC lab does not run 24/7 so the contractor shall provide a system by which their AODs (Administrative Officer of the Day) can monitor the system remotely 24 hours per day. Provide self-contained, continuous, computerized, automated monitoring of blood culture bottles with immediate, active (e.g. audible alarm) notification of microorganism growth based upon pre-programmed criteria and notification of termination of maximum programmed incubation period when no microorganism growth is detected. Allow for operator extension of programmed incubation times while testing is in progress, without interruption of automatic continuous monitoring. Have the capability to monitor the blood volume in each culture bottle. Utilize sufficient safety features to avoid unnecessary exposure to biohazardous and chemical material. The exposure to and the volume of biohazardous and chemical material generated by the equipment must be minimal and require a minimum amount of handling. Have the capability to detect and document elapsed time to positivity. Have bar code reading capability to eliminate the need for manual entry of patient information for each sample. Contractor bar code formats shall meet requirements of VA lab information system software. Have the capability to scan the culture vial sequence and specimen accession label in any order. This proposed contract action is for a service in which the Government intends to award a firm fixed-price STAT Reference Lab Testing Services contract with only one source; Kaleida Health, 726 Exchange Street, Buffalo, NY 14210 under the authority Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 6.302-1 Only One Responsible Source. Places of Performance: Department of Veterans Affairs Buffalo VAMC Laboratory Department 3495 Bailey Avenue Buffalo, NY 14215 Purpose and Objectives: The intent of this Special Notice is to identify potential offerors capable of providing analysis, monitoring, and reporting findings of laboratory and pathology tests for the VA Upstate NY Healthcare System at Buffalo VAMC. Contractor shall provide STAT laboratory testing on Veteran patient specimens seven days a week, including holidays, 24 hours a day. Contractor laboratory requires mandatory licensing and accreditation possessing a NYS Department of Health Clinical Laboratory Permit, Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) License and College of American Pathologists (CAP) Accreditation. General Requirements The Contractor must be able to perform all of the required testing as follows: a. Contractor will provide STAT laboratory testing on patient specimens seven days a week, including holidays, 24 hours a day. b. VA will be responsible for specimen collection, preparation, preservation, and delivery, except for semen analysis which will be delivered by the patient to contractor location. c. Sample analysis for routine laboratory testing will be performed as soon as possible by the contractor. Results will be faxed to the VA with originals to follow by mail or courier. d. Sample analysis for STAT laboratory testing will be reported within two hours after sample delivery. Results will be reported via phone and faxed, with originals to follow by mail or courier. e. Tests in addition to the specified list may be required on a rare occasion if a need arises to send a sample to be tested locally for expedited patient care. This will be limited to testing that can be performed in house at the contractor site. Response: Responses to this Special Notice should be able to demonstrate the firm's ability, capability, and responsibility to deliver the service listed above. The purpose of this Special Notice announcement is for market research to make appropriate acquisition decisions and to gain knowledge of potential qualified Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses, Veteran Owned Small Businesses, 8(a), HubZone and other Small Businesses interested and capable of providing the services described above. Documentation of technical expertise must be presented in sufficient detail for the Government to determine that your company possesses the necessary functional area expertise and experience to compete for this acquisition.
